Sun diagrams can be used to find elevation and azimuth of the sun for any point of time for a given location. Architects use them to plan for lighting, heating and air conditioning. But it can also be useful to as an alternative to magnetic compasses in navigation or just to check sunset and sunrise times or when a shadow will hit a certain point.

This app takes either the latitude your entered or acquires it from your current location and draws the sun diagram either for the whole year or for the month you chose.

Currently, Boeing is running an advertisement campaign in Denmark, because the danish airforce is about to spend 30 billion DKK on new fighter-jets. They are advertising for the near-ancient F/A 18 Super Hornet (they even made a [site](http://www.superhornet.dk) to promote it ([Archived](https://archive.is/u5jHO))).

It's all over.. Bus-stops, local radio, TV, youtube.. everywhere..

They are not just advertising to our elected representatives - they are targeting the population.

I started to wonder if it is even legal. We have a ban on tobacco and alcohol advertisements in the public space - but war machines are okay? Apparently we are not part of the [EASA ](http://www.easa-alliance.org/)so their guidelines are not bringing me closer to an answer.

I skimmed over some of the danish laws for 'war material' production - but it doesn't say anything about advertisement.

It pisses me off - and wish I could find a way to block the whole deal from happening.
Alcohol and tobacco harms everyone whilst arms hurt only the enemy?

Are political ads not allowed? Your country is in the process of replacing its F-16s and the alternatives you're looking at are the much more expensive F-35 and Typhoon, which are both only about 5 years newer than the Super Hornet. Are Lockheed-Martin and Eurofighter not advertising as well?

Edit: You might also be experiencing the Baader-Meinhoff phenomenon where you see a thing everywhere because it became relevant to you.

Political ads, yes - if you have a party. Last I checked, Boeing was not a political candidate in any danish elections I can remember (that might change though).

Neither Lockheed-Martin or Airbus is advertising. Lockheed doesn't need to, since we're part of the JSF project already. Airbus is European and, I guess, have a slightly different approach to advertising than US based Boeing.

To be honest, I have not been exposed to more than one radio advert. But then again, I live a very secluded life, away from the chaos of the real world - so my exposure is very low.

That said - from what I can read, hear and see in danish media - it's all over the place.

I don't really care who gets the contract (and if we absolutely have to buy war machines - how about a fleet of drones instead?). I do however care about how you indirectly manipulate politicians through the population. Especially when it comes to 'products' like this.

The danish population really shouldn't have a say in this. It's why we elect officials in the first place - because the average citizen has absolutely no clue what the best option is. They will look at the promise of 10.000 jobs, and think "Hey, that Boeing thing sounds like a really good idea - let's support that." - which in turn will affect the choice that the politicians will make (popular opinion and all that).

Not that kind of political ad. It falls under lobbying laws, which are very lax in Denmark.

Drones apparently aren't on the table for you guys. Just a choice between those three planes. And the ones you have now, of course.

Thanks for pointing that out - didn't realize that it fell under lobbying laws. Doesn't make it more acceptable though. And didn't think you were allowed to 'lobby' towards the population.

Edit: SAAB Gripen was on the table too - but was ignored/withdrawn.
